Und wo mitgeschrieben wird, wächst die Status-Datei in Monaten zu einem Tagebuch, in dem der aktuelle Stand zwischen Erledigtem verschwindet.

Die nächste Session liest das und macht weiter.

session-handoff.whyBuilt: Ich arbeite an mehreren Projekten parallel und selten zwei Tage am Stück am selben. Dateien lösen das: sie überleben jeden Kontext-Reset und du kannst sie lesen, ohne ein Tool zu starten.

fable-prompter.tagline: Denk mit Opus, arbeite mit Fable: ein Prompt, der präzise sitzt und Tokens spart.
fable-prompter.subheading: Lass Opus 5 aus deiner groben Idee den Prompt bauen und schick ihn in Fable 5 ab – die Rechenarbeit landet dort, wo sie hingehört.
bullets: Spart Tokens und Runden: die Idee steht so präzise drin, dass Fable nicht raten und nachfragen muss
Nutzt aus, was Fable 5 anders macht – Ziel statt Schrittfolge, Initiative mit klaren Grenzen
Fertig zum Abschicken: kein Ausfüllfeld, keine eckigen Klammern, kein Nachbessern
Setzt Leitplanken, wo Eigeninitiative teuer wird – besonders in Cowork mit echten Dateien
fable-prompter.note: Führ diesen Skill mit Opus 5 aus, nicht mit Fable 5. Opus baut den Prompt, Fable arbeitet ihn ab. Andersherum lässt du das teure Nachdenken vom Modell erledigen, das eigentlich nur ausführen sollte – und zahlst es in Tokens.
fable-prompter.problem: Ein vager Prompt kostet dich zwei Dinge: Runden und Tokens. Fable fragt nach, rät falsch, du korrigierst, es rechnet erneut. Dazu kommen die Prompt-Gewohnheiten von 2024, die heute aktiv schaden – durchnummerierte Schrittfolgen, Freigabe-Schleifen, "denk Schritt für Schritt". Sie machen das Ergebnis schlechter, nicht besser.

howItWorks.title: Installieren
howItWorks.body: Skill herunterladen und in deinem AI-Assistenten einbinden.

howItWorks.title: Den Prompt von Opus 5 bauen lassen
howItWorks.body: Führ diesen Skill mit Opus 5 aus, nicht mit Fable. Wirf eine grobe Idee rein, einen vagen Auftrag, einen Absatz Kontext – oder einen alten Prompt, der nicht mehr zieht. Opus denkt die Aufgabe durch und formuliert sie präzise aus.

howItWorks.title: Prompt in Fable 5 abschicken
howItWorks.body: Ein einzelner Codeblock, fertig zum Kopieren – kein Vorwort, keine eckigen Klammern. Die Denkarbeit ist dann schon erledigt, Fable führt nur noch aus. Genau so nutzt du dein Token-Budget sinnvoll.

fable-prompter.whyBuilt: Ich habe zu viele Prompts gesehen, die aus lauter Vorsicht überstrukturiert waren und dadurch schlechter liefen. Und ich habe zu oft zugesehen, wie ein starkes Modell erst mal rät, was ich eigentlich will. Beides kostet Geld. Der Skill trennt die zwei Arbeiten sauber: Opus denkt, Fable macht.
builtFor: Erstellen mit Opus 5 · Ausführen in Fable 5

linkedin-content-creation.subheading: The angle first, then the text – and you decide in between. Hook first, every number flagged, an edit pass with fresh eyes.
bullets: Your raw material gets used instead of gathering dust: voice memo, video, PDF, link
You decide twice – nothing goes through to the finished text without your say-so
No invented evidence: every number in the draft carries a fact-check marker
No recycling of your own phrasing – every post gets its own texture
linkedin-content-creation.problem: The raw material for good posts is already there: in voice memos, calls, PDFs. What comes out of it is usually generic or a week too late. And if you just let the AI run, you end up with a text nobody would have signed off – with numbers nobody checked.

howItWorks.title: Install
howItWorks.body: Download the skill and add it to your AI assistant. It contains two skills: the workflow and the writing engine.

howItWorks.title: Drop in material
howItWorks.body: Voice memo, video, PDF, link or a rough idea. Audio is transcribed locally. On the first run, the skill sets up your linkedin/ folder together with you.

howItWorks.title: Decide twice
howItWorks.body: First the angle, then the draft. At both points the skill stops and waits for your say-so – you sharpen or approve. Your final version is saved as a version of its own: the difference between draft and final text is what the next post learns from.

linkedin-content-creation.whyBuilt: I write posts for clients and for myself. The problem was never the writing, but the angle and the discipline: don’t recycle, don’t claim anything nobody has checked, and don’t overwrite the draft – because the difference between draft and final version is the only thing the system learns from.

jour-fixe.tagline: The hour of meeting prep that comes back every week – done before you sit down.
jour-fixe.subheading: Pulls your sources, checks last week against what actually happened and builds the deck – only after you’ve approved it.
bullets: You walk in prepared: no more scraping together hours, tasks and last week’s deck
Finds the gap before the meeting – every priority without progress comes to you as a question first
Runs on your own sources: time tracking, last deck, task board, verbal updates
Deck in your format: Gamma, Markdown, slide text or document
jour-fixe.problem: The recurring meeting eats the same hour every week: gathering sources, remembering what was promised last week, building slides. And the one point with nothing to report only hits you in the meeting – in front of the client.

howItWorks.title: Install
howItWorks.body: Download the skill and add it to your AI assistant.

howItWorks.title: Add your sources
howItWorks.body: On the first run the skill asks for your sources – time tracking, last deck, task board – and creates a config from them. After that it reads them itself every week.

howItWorks.title: Check, approve, generate
howItWorks.body: First the check with open questions, then the slide draft in the chat. The deck only gets built once you say so.

jour-fixe.whyBuilt: The value of this meeting hinges on a single point: the honest comparison between what was planned and what actually happened. Everything else is formatting. So the skill does the comparison first – and asks, instead of glossing over a gap.

session-handoff.tagline: Give your AI a memory: what happened, where you stand, why you decided the way you did.
session-handoff.subheading: From now on, things get written down. Every session ends with a status the next one reads – across /clear, model switches and weeks off.
bullets: No more starting from nothing: the next session knows where you left off
Your decisions and the reasons behind them survive every /clear and every model switch
The status stays readable: a dashboard on one screen, not an overgrown diary
No service, no database, no subscription – three Markdown files in your own project
session-handoff.problem: AI sessions forget everything. Next time you open one, you explain your project from scratch – or worse: the AI makes a decision again that you already made and justified three weeks ago. And where things do get written down, the status file grows over the months into a diary in which the current state disappears among finished items.

howItWorks.title: Install
howItWorks.body: Download the skill and add it to your AI assistant. It comes with the /handoff command.

howItWorks.title: Trigger it at the end of a session
howItWorks.body: Say "handoff" or type /handoff while the conversation’s context is still alive. If the structure doesn’t exist yet, the skill sets it up with you.

howItWorks.title: From now on your project has a memory
howItWorks.body: Three files that never overlap: status.md says where you stand. log.md, what happened. decisions.md, why you decided the way you did – and the skill writes nothing in there that you haven’t read and approved first. The next session reads it and carries on.

session-handoff.whyBuilt: I work on several projects in parallel and rarely two days in a row on the same one. The most expensive moment was always getting back in – and the times a fresh session reopened a decision made long ago because its reasoning wasn’t written down anywhere. Files solve that: they survive every context reset, and you can read them without starting a tool.
builtFor: Claude Code (skill + /handoff command)
Any project with files – no service, no database
Sets up the structure itself if you want

fable-prompter.tagline: Think with Opus, work with Fable: a prompt that lands precisely and saves tokens.
fable-prompter.subheading: Let Opus 5 build the prompt from your rough idea and send it off in Fable 5 – the heavy computing happens where it belongs.
bullets: Saves tokens and rounds: the idea is spelled out so precisely that Fable doesn’t have to guess or ask
Uses what Fable 5 does differently – a goal instead of a sequence of steps, initiative within clear limits
Ready to send: no fill-in fields, no square brackets, no touch-ups
Sets guardrails where initiative gets expensive – especially in Cowork with real files
fable-prompter.note: Run this skill with Opus 5, not Fable 5. Opus builds the prompt, Fable works through it. The other way round, you let the model that should only be executing do the expensive thinking – and you pay for it in tokens.
fable-prompter.problem: A vague prompt costs you two things: rounds and tokens. Fable asks back, guesses wrong, you correct it, it computes again. On top of that come the prompt habits of 2024 that actively hurt today – numbered step sequences, approval loops, "think step by step". They make the result worse, not better.

howItWorks.title: Install
howItWorks.body: Download the skill and add it to your AI assistant.

howItWorks.title: Let Opus 5 build the prompt
howItWorks.body: Run this skill with Opus 5, not with Fable. Drop in a rough idea, a vague task, a paragraph of context – or an old prompt that doesn’t work any more. Opus thinks the task through and spells it out precisely.

howItWorks.title: Send the prompt in Fable 5
howItWorks.body: A single code block, ready to copy – no preamble, no square brackets. The thinking is already done; Fable only executes. That’s how you spend your token budget well.

fable-prompter.whyBuilt: I’ve seen too many prompts that were over-structured out of sheer caution and ran worse because of it. And I’ve watched too often as a strong model first guesses what I actually want. Both cost money. The skill separates the two jobs cleanly: Opus thinks, Fable does.
builtFor: Build with Opus 5 · run in Fable 5
Chat and Cowork – not for the API
